items.title: Introducing Evo Agentic AppSec: Security That Keeps Up With AI Development
items.summary: AI-driven development is outpacing traditional security workflows. Snyk’s Agentic AppSec uses security agents to find, fix, and verify vulnerabilities continuously, while humans set the bar.

items.title: VulnBump: Can AI Agents Fix Vulnerable Dependencies Without Breaking the Build?
items.summary: VulnBump tests AI agents on 307 real dependency upgrades. A fix counts only if the vulnerability is gone and the build and tests stay green.

items.title: Frontier models found the vulnerabilities. Only the attacker found the chains.
items.summary: Static analysis found the flaws, but only live attack testing proved how they could be chained into breaches. A comparison of Evo COS, Claude Security, and Claude Code Security.

items.title: Autonomous Attacks Are Already Here. The Defense Has to Match Their Speed.
items.summary: Autonomous attackers are shrinking the window for defense. Learn how continuous discovery, remediation, validation, and prevention can help security teams keep pace.

items.title: Why AI Coding Agents Keep Writing Broken Access Control
items.summary: AI coding agents can produce authorization logic that compiles and passes review while exposing one tenant’s data to another. Learn why broken access control is difficult to detect and how to prevent it.

items.title: What Is Agentic AppSec?
items.summary: Learn how Agentic AppSec uses grounded, bounded, and independently verified AI agents to run the application security loop.

items.title: Evo ADS Govern Agent Behavior Goes GA: Bringing MCP Usage Under Control
items.summary: Evo ADS Govern Agent Behavior is now generally available, starting with MCP Governance. Discover, approve, monitor, log, and block MCP server usage across leading AI coding agents.

items.title: Your Vulnerability Backlog Is No Longer Technical Debt, It’s an Attack Surface
items.summary: A growing vulnerability backlog is more than technical debt: it is an attack surface. Learn why outdated risk assumptions, automated attackers, and chained findings demand a new approach.

items.title: So I asked my agent instead…
items.summary: Ask your Evo tenant about models, MCP servers, and skills across your AI estate, from the client you already work in.

items.title: The AI Hurricane Is Here
items.summary: AI is accelerating software creation and cyberattacks alike. Leaders must secure agents and code at inception, enforce controls at runtime, and validate defenses independently.

items.title: Is prevention essentially a solved problem?
items.summary: Prevention in agent-generated code is architecturally solved—but choosing controls that protect security without slowing development remains the challenge.

items.title: Why Your AI Application Is Exposed (Even When Your Scans Come Back Clean)
items.summary: AI applications can pass security scans yet remain exploitable through chained attacks across models, tools, data, and business workflows. Learn how DAST, AI pentesting, and red teaming work together to expose end-to-end risk.

items.title: Remediation Agents, Demystified: Why Fixing Beats Finding
items.summary: See how Snyk’s Remediation Agent uses security intelligence, breakability analysis, and validation to turn vulnerabilities into mergeable pull requests.

items.title: Benchmarking Secure-and-Functional Remediation and How Snyk Agent Fix Lifts Frontier-Model Fix Rates by over 14%
items.summary: A benchmark of secure, functional vulnerability fixes across JavaScript, Java, and Python shows Snyk Intelligence helps frontier models break past a 72–75% performance plateau.

items.title: The Agent Baseline: 35 Controls, But Where Should You Start?
items.summary: The Agent Baseline defines 35 controls across six security outcomes—but the right starting point depends on how your organization uses agents. Learn how to sequence controls for coding, internal, and production agents.
